Following the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III apply starting 2 December 2027.
Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) apply starting 2 August 2028.

Before the AI Omnibus amendment, the AI Act as adopted in 2024 provided that high-risk AI system obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) would apply 36 months after entry into force, i.e. 2 August 2026.

Article 113/Article 111 of the AI Act (as consolidated) provides that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before the date of application of Chapter III only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) references 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' rather than stating 2 August 2026 explicitly, reflecting the post-Omnibus amendment that removed the fixed 2026 date.

The Commission proposed adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available; Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification on 7 May 2026.

As of a source published 9 April 2026 (120 days before 2 August 2026), the obligations for high-risk AI systems (Annex III) were described as taking effect on 2 August 2026, with no mention of the Omnibus delay having taken effect.

A commentary notes that if the Omnibus amendments were not approved and enacted before 2 August 2026, the high-risk AI provisions would, under the law as it stood, technically apply from that date (2 August 2026), creating timeline pressure to finalize the amendments beforehand.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8 to 15 of the AI Act and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 enter into application and are enforceable from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy systems to comply with Article 50(2) marking/detection obligations.

Under the AI Act as originally adopted in 2024, the Regulation was to be fully applicable 24 months after entry into force (i.e., August 2026), with high-risk system obligations applicable 36 months after entry into force.
The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025 and governance/GPAI obligations applying from 2 August 2025.

# EU AI Act: When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply?

## Executive Summary
The obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act were originally scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, but this timeline has been amended by the AI Omnibus Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As a result, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, while obligations for high-risk systems embedded in products under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as adopted in 2024 provided that high-risk AI system obligations under Chapter III, Sections 1–3, would apply 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). Under this original schedule, the Regulation as a whole was intended to be fully applicable 24 months after entry into force, with high-risk obligations following at the 36-month mark (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
Delayed availability of harmonised standards put the original 2 August 2026 deadline in jeopardy, prompting legislative action to extend it (medium confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). The Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms that needed standards and tools are available; the Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification on 7 May 2026 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The AI Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 — just days before the original deadline (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk systems embedded in Annex I-covered products (under Union harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text now refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than stating 2 August 2026 explicitly, reflecting removal of the fixed 2026 date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Article 111 (as consolidated) provides that operators of high-risk systems already placed on the market before the Chapter III application date are covered only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy systems regarding marking/detection obligations (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-related AI also begin applying around 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant split exists between sources reflecting pre-Omnibus law (stating 2 August 2026) and those incorporating the amendment (stating 2 December 2027). This largely reflects publication timing rather than substantive disagreement, since the Omnibus entered into force only shortly before the original deadline. One commentary (low confidence, flagged below 0.4) frames 2 August 2026 as a contingent "backstop" date had the Omnibus not passed in time ([LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this is superseded by confirmation that the Omnibus did enter into force on 27 July 2026. Similarly, a low-confidence source dated 9 April 2026 still described 2 August 2026 as the applicable date without acknowledging the pending delay ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now a fixed deadline or still conditional on Commission confirmation that standards and tools are available, as originally proposed. It is also unconfirmed whether all EUR-Lex cross-references have been fully updated to remove the superseded 2026 date, and whether sector-specific national guidance has caught up with the Omnibus changes, given several lower-authority sources still cite the outdated deadline.

# EU AI Act: When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply?

## Executive Summary
The obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act were originally scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, but this timeline has been amended by the AI Omnibus Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As a result, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, while obligations for high-risk systems embedded in products under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as adopted in 2024 provided that high-risk AI system obligations under Chapter III, Sections 1–3, would apply 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). Under this original schedule, the Regulation as a whole was intended to be fully applicable 24 months after entry into force, with high-risk obligations following at the 36-month mark (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
Delayed availability of harmonised standards put the original 2 August 2026 deadline in jeopardy, prompting legislative action to extend it (medium confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). The Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms that needed standards and tools are available; the Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification on 7 May 2026 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The AI Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 — just days before the original deadline (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk systems embedded in Annex I-covered products (under Union harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text now refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than stating 2 August 2026 explicitly, reflecting removal of the fixed 2026 date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Article 111 (as consolidated) provides that operators of high-risk systems already placed on the market before the Chapter III application date are covered only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy systems regarding marking/detection obligations (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-related AI also begin applying around 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant split exists between sources reflecting pre-Omnibus law (stating 2 August 2026) and those incorporating the amendment (stating 2 December 2027). This largely reflects publication timing rather than substantive disagreement, since the Omnibus entered into force only shortly before the original deadline. One commentary (low confidence, flagged below 0.4) frames 2 August 2026 as a contingent "backstop" date had the Omnibus not passed in time ([LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this is superseded by confirmation that the Omnibus did enter into force on 27 July 2026. Similarly, a low-confidence source dated 9 April 2026 still described 2 August 2026 as the applicable date without acknowledging the pending delay ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now a fixed deadline or still conditional on Commission confirmation that standards and tools are available, as originally proposed. It is also unconfirmed whether all EUR-Lex cross-references have been fully updated to remove the superseded 2026 date, and whether sector-specific national guidance has caught up with the Omnibus changes, given several lower-authority sources still cite the outdated deadline.
